*** THE GILT IS THE STORY, AND THE MOVE WAS MONDAY'S NOT THIS MORNING'S ***
The ten-year gilt stands at 5.43%. That is about six basis points above the 5.37% this brief published
on Monday morning, and the rise happened during Monday's session: CNBC's previous close is 5.4369 and
the live reading is 5.4324, so TODAY's change is about half a basis point, effectively flat.
PUBLISHED: 5.43, -0.01. The distinction matters because a ticker reports the change on the day, and
writing +0.06 would imply the move is happening now when it happened yesterday. The six-basis-point
rise belongs in the prose, not the change field. Trading Economics agrees: 5.43, change -0.010.
Context worth stating: this is eight days before the Budget and the gilt is near its highest since 2007.

*** TWO CLOSES WHERE THE FEED'S PREVIOUS-CLOSE FIELD IS SELF-REFERENTIAL ***
  S&P: last 7,690.73 with previous_day_closing also 7,690.73. The +0.41% in the change field is
       Monday's move and is used; the prev field is ignored.
  VIX: last 18.44 with prev also 18.44 and the change reported as "UNCH". Computed by hand against
       Friday's close of 19.99, which this brief published twice over the weekend: -7.75%.
       So volatility fell nearly eight per cent on Monday. Declared as a computed figure.

*** BRENT: BACK ABOVE 110, AND TRADING ECONOMICS IS NOW UNUSABLE ENTIRELY ***
CNBC @LCO.1 110.58, +0.94% against a previous settle of 109.55, stamped 07:10 today. Oil has reversed
the whole of yesterday's fall and more: 107.57 at this time yesterday, 109.55 at Monday's settle,
110.58 now. No approved source explains it as at the time of compilation and no cause is attributed.
Trading Economics returns 98.78 with a change of +0.24% — the level is now about twelve dollars below
CNBC, the sixth consecutive day its Brent page has been wrong, and today even the CHANGE diverges
(+0.24 against +0.94). Unlike previous days it corroborates nothing, so it is discarded entirely and
Brent rests on CNBC alone.
